description:
It's one of Africa's longest running conflicts.
The dispute over the territory of Western Sahara started more than 50 years ago. 
It began with the end of Spanish colonial rule in the region. 
Since then, both Morocco and the Polisario Front have claimed Western Sahara. 
But in the 1990s, the UN tried to reach a settlement and deployed a peacekeeping mission to the region.
Last week, those efforts ended, when Russia and the US blocked proposals to extend its mandate.
So, could this development lead to renewed fighting?

Presenter: Imran Khan

Guests
Samir Bennis, political analyst and author of "The Self-Determination Delusion: How Activist Scholars and Journalists Have Hijacked the Western Sahara Case". 
Irene Fernandez-Molina, Senior Lecturer in International Relations at the University of Exeter, UK and author of "Moroccan Foreign Policy under Mohammed VI, 1999-2014"
Mahjoub Mleiha, Advocacy Head of CODESA -  Collective of Sahrawi Human Rights Defenders

The temporary truce was brokered with the involvement of US First Lady Melania Trump, with Pope Leo also supporting efforts to secure humanitarian access. It enabled civilians to leave the frontline town and provided a brief window for supplies to reach residents facing severe shortages of food, medicine and clean water.

Ukrainian and Russian officials said the operation enabled cooperation despite the continuing war. Pope Leo has expressed hope that the agreement could encourage further dialogue, but the end of the truce leaves uncertainty for civilians who remain in Oleshky.

The ceasefire was a local humanitarian arrangement, not a broader end to the fighting between Russia and Ukraine.

In a dramatic development ahead of the US midterm elections, Democratic Congresswoman Haley Stevens has endorsed Republican Mike Rogers in Michigan's closely contested Senate race, rejecting her party's nominee, Abdul El-Sayed. Stevens had previously pledged to support El-Sayed, but their relationship deteriorated after he refused to denounce an advert criticising US support for Israel's war in Gaza. President Donald Trump praised Stevens for crossing party lines while attacking El-Sayed over his Muslim faith. The endorsement has exposed divisions among Michigan Democrats, who accuse Stevens of undermining their candidate and helping Rogers, whom they link to Trump. Rogers has welcomed the support, although it remains unclear whether the endorsement will influence voters with just one full day of campaigning left.
